result.title: World Action Critic (WAC) Model: Joint Foresight and Criticism for Policy Learning
result.summary: World models have shown considerable promise in sequential decision-making by anticipating the consequences of actions and providing predictive foresight for policy learning. However, learning to reason about counterfactual actions remains challenging, since predictive objectives may underemphasize information critical for action evaluation, while unexecuted actions lack observed futures for direct supervision. To address these challenges, we propose the World Action Critic (WAC) Model, which proposes multimodal action candidates and jointly learns candidate-conditioned future prediction and consequence evaluation. In our proposed framework, critic supervision directly shapes intermediate predictive representations during rollout, encouraging them to retain information needed to distinguish action quality. Observed futures supervise prediction for executed actions, while external task-quality targets provide evaluation signals for counterfactual candidates. Through joint optimization, critic signals from these candidates propagate into predictive representations without requiring their observed futures. Our theoretical analysis characterizes critic-guided feature retention and bounds candidate-selection regret. Applied to autonomous driving, WAC achieves 93.4 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly learning predictive foresight and consequence evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 World Action Critic 模型，在多模态动作候选上联合学习候选条件下的未来预测与后果评估，让 critic 信号塑造中间预测表示，并在自动驾驶 NAVSIM-v1 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「critic 监督直接作用于中间预测表示、促使其保留动作判别信息」的训练机制，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及外部评价信号如何塑造内部表示与缓解信息坍缩，但属较远的自动驾驶世界模型领域，迁移性待验证。
